views.label: All
views.note: HTTP, WS and SSE cross the edge into the hexagon; cmd/api and cmd/worker are one image, Postgres is the only state, the vendor is a port.

views.label: Auth
views.note: Signup, verify and login ride the slices; codes and sessions persist in Postgres, access JWTs never leave the response.

views.label: Realtime
views.note: WS /api/v1/ws?token= closes 4001 on a bad token; SSE flushes hub events per write and dies with the request context.

views.label: Ops
views.note: readyz pings the pool; migrations are a separate goose step, never startup; the worker claims email_jobs with SKIP LOCKED.

boundaries.label: The <app> runtime — one image, two entrypoints
State plane — the only persistence boundary

cards.title: The three skills
items: skills/go-best-practices loads on every Go edit and carries the stack contract digest (references/backend-go-stack.md)
skills/go-review writes a prioritized report where every finding cites the rule it breaks and shows the fix
skills/go-port ports any language to idiomatic Go, porting the original tests first so behavior is provable

cards.title: The stack it teaches
items: Go 1.27 stdlib net/http: method + wildcard ServeMux matching, no router library
pgx/v5 pool opened once at the composition root; sqlc compiles per-slice queries.sql into committed internal/gen/db
goose annotated reversible migrations applied by go tool goose — never at server startup (readyz catches drift)

cards.title: The lint law
items: lints/ is a drop-in golangci-lint v2 config whose depguard rules are the architecture: domain-pure, slice-isolation
every rule in the config is proven to fire against the check module in lints/check/
slog is the only logging dependency; otel is deliberately cut — ctx-first seams make it an addition, not a refactor
